question: Do the 'Report' entries in the MINIMUM and MAXIMUM limit columns for Cyanide, Total Recoverable and Total Dissolved Solids establish enforceable numeric discharge limits, or do they indicate report-only requirements for which no numeric compliance comparison applies?
semantic_arguments: Meaning of 'Report' in the MINIMUM and MAXIMUM columns of the DISCHARGE LIMITATIONS table versus numeric limit values
Contrast with other pollutants in the same table that specify numeric MAXIMUM values (e.g., Total Suspended Solids MONTHLY AVG 20 and DAILY MAX 30 mg/l)
Whether a reporting-only entry in the limitations columns creates an enforceable numeric limit or only a reporting obligation
Table structure separating EFFLUENT CHARACTERISTICS limit columns (lbs/day and mg/l MINIMUM/MAXIMUM) from MONITORING REQUIREMENTS columns
notes: The target spans list 'Report' in all MINIMUM and MAXIMUM cells for both pollutants. Purpose A requires distinguishing enforceable numeric limits from report-only monitoring; different readings of 'Report' in the limit columns would change whether reported measurements are subject to numeric exceedance evaluation.
